Titel: [ARFC] Deploy [PROJECT] V4 on Base

## Summary

This ARFC seeks community feedback on deploying [PROJECT] V4 on Base and activating an initial tokenized equities market.

Base is an Ethereum Layer 2 incubated by Coinbase, with low transaction costs, native USDC liquidity, and access to a broad retail user base. [PROJECT] has operated on Base since [YEAR], and the network was among [PROJECT]'s first multi-chain deployments to surpass $1 billion in deposits.

The deployment would bring the Hub and Spoke architecture to one of [PROJECT]'s largest existing deployments. It would establish a dedicated Equities Hub, separating liquidity and risk for the tokenized equities market from other [PROJECT] markets on Base, while providing a foundation for specialized markets as the network develops.

## Motivation

Base combines an established [PROJECT] deployment, growing stablecoin activity, and an expanding set of consumer applications, payments products, and trading venues. These conditions support demand for onchain credit infrastructure that can serve distinct use cases while maintaining clearly defined liquidity and risk boundaries.

Deploying [PROJECT] V4 on Base would:

* Upgrade one of [PROJECT]'s largest existing deployments to the current protocol architecture.
* Establish a dedicated market for tokenized equities, with USDC as the borrowable asset and tokenized equities used exclusively as collateral at launch.
* Separate the liquidity and risk of this market from other [PROJECT] markets on Base through a dedicated Equities Hub.
* Extend [PROJECT]'s presence within the Base and Coinbase ecosystem as additional users, applications, and tokenized assets come onchain.

The initial market provides a focused implementation of the V4 architecture. A single pooled spoke will support the initial set of tokenized equities as collateral, allowing users to borrow USDC against diversified positions while maintaining asset-specific collateral factors. The equities themselves will not be borrowable at launch.

Coinbase's distribution, infrastructure, and institutional relationships may support a broader range of tokenized assets on Base over time. A dedicated V4 market provides a measured starting point for this activity, with a market structure designed to accommodate distinct collateral types and risk profiles without extending their exposure to other [PROJECT] markets.

## Market Structure

The tokenized equities market is deployed through a dedicated Equities Hub on Base. USDC suppliers to the hub explicitly opt into lending against tokenized equity collateral, and this exposure is isolated from other [PROJECT] markets.

The Hub contains a single USDC reserve and two spokes. The Mag-7 Spoke supports USDC borrowing against the seven specified tokenized equities. The Tokenized USDC Spoke is supply only, providing vaults and aggregators with a composable USDC position without collateral exposure.

Within the Mag-7 Spoke, users may supply any combination of the seven tokenized equities as collateral and borrow USDC. Each asset retains its own collateral factor, so borrowing capacity remains determined by the composition of each position. Pooling the assets within one spoke allows diversified collateral positions to be managed within a single market.

The tokenized equities are collateral only at launch. Borrowing of equities, and positions that borrow one equity against another, are not enabled.

Titel: [PROJECT] Alliance BORG Foundation Update: Appointment of Leeward Supervisors Limited as Supervisor

### TL;DR

This vote seeks [PROJECT] DAO approval for the appointment of [Leeward Supervisors Limited ("Leeward")]([URL] as Supervisor of [[PROJECT] Alliance BORG Foundation ("[PROJECT] Alliance BORG")]([URL]

Leeward is a Cayman Islands governance, compliance and fiduciary services firm specialising in Web3 and digital assets, and the current Supervisor of [PROJECT] Labs Foundation. Through that role, it is already familiar with the structure and functions of the entities operating adjacent to [PROJECT] DAO.

### Background

[PROJECT] Alliance BORG is a Cayman Islands foundation company established to support the purposes assigned to it under its governing documents as approved by [PROJECT] DAO. It has no members or beneficiaries, and its business and affairs are managed by or under the control of its board of directors. It is funded through [the Ecosystem Grant gRequest (EGG)]([URL]

Under the [[PROJECT] Alliance BORG Bylaws]([URL] as [amended]([URL] [PROJECT] Alliance BORG must have at least one Supervisor at all times, as required for a memberless Cayman Islands foundation company. The Supervisor is responsible for holding the board of directors accountable and overseeing compliance with the foundation company's constitutional documents and applicable law.

The Supervisor is responsible for enforcing [PROJECT] Alliance BORG's rules and has the right and power to hold BORG Personnel liable for:

- Any fraud or violation of applicable Legal Requirements committed by or on behalf of [PROJECT] Alliance BORG, or on behalf of BORG Personnel in connection with [PROJECT] Alliance BORG's activities.
- Any knowing and intentional material breach of a material term of the Governance Agreements by [PROJECT] Alliance BORG or BORG Personnel that could reasonably be expected to materially adversely impact [PROJECT] Alliance BORG or the Community, or any part of the Community.

The current Supervisor of [PROJECT] Alliance BORG is [MetaLeX Pro, LLP]([URL] which was appointed on a temporary basis. MetaLeX Pro, LLP has provided [notice of its resignation]([URL] as Supervisor, to take effect upon the appointment of a new Supervisor. Accordingly, [PROJECT] Alliance BORG now proposes appointing a new entity to this role.

### Proposal

Approve the appointment of Leeward Supervisors Limited as Supervisor of [PROJECT] Alliance BORG.

If this proposal is approved:

- The board of [PROJECT] Alliance BORG will complete the necessary corporate actions to give effect to Leeward's appointment, in accordance with [PROJECT] Alliance BORG's governing documents.
- Upon Leeward's appointment becoming effective, MetaLeX Pro, LLP will resign as the current Supervisor.

Auswahl: For / Against

Titel: [PROJECT] Security Program

# [PROJECT] Security Program

## Abstract

The [PROJECT] Foundation proposes to continue and evolve the [PROJECT] Audit Program (AAP) - [launched on [DATE]]([URL] with a one-year mandate - into a broader [PROJECT] Security Program (ASP), running for a further 12 months on a rolling-application basis.

- **From "Audit" to "Security".** AAP delivered on its original purpose - real vulnerabilities surfaced and remediated before mainnet, with a high share of net-new teams brought to [PROJECT] - and demonstrated where subsidised security converts into the most ecosystem value. Building on that, the mandate broadens to four pillars covering the full security lifecycle: AI-assisted screening ahead of a full audit, the human-conducted audit itself, the [PROJECT] bug bounty program, and the ArbitrumDAO Security Council.

- **No new treasury request.** ~$2M in cumulative audit commitments is expected by AAP's close. The remaining $1.76M USDC + 25M [TOKEN] held by the Foundation becomes ASP's operational budget, less ~$1.2M in predicted outstanding deployments.

- **Operational refinements from a year of experience.** The audit committee technical expert retainer is right-sized to $2.5k/month based on expected workload; the [DAO-approved]([URL] alignment framework is maintained as the program's baseline; program changes adopt a lightweight optimistic approval process to reduce governance overhead; and idle funds are put to work in low-risk management strategies.

The program runs for one year (or until funds are exhausted), managed by the [PROJECT] Foundation and supported by the audit committee as technical SME, with quarterly transparency reports and a final summary report to the DAO.

## Motivation

The AAP was [approved by ArbitrumDAO]([URL] to remove a barrier facing early-stage teams: third-party audits are the industry norm, but their cost puts them out of reach for many young projects. The program's full design - objectives, eligibility, application process, auditor approval, and alignment commitments including [PROJECT] exclusivity - is set out in the original proposal, and its performance has been reported quarterly ([#1]([URL] [#2]([URL] [#3]([URL]

### Results

*(covering Q1-Q3 and preliminary Q4, prior to final report)*

367 applications were received through preliminary Q4, with application-to-decision time averaging 2-3 weeks. To date, 18 completed audits reviewed 71,366 lines of code and identified 385 vulnerabilities - 13 critical and 40 high - remediated before mainnet. The average audit cost was $50,706, approximately $15 per line of code, which sits below the industry average of $70,000 for mid-complexity DeFi audits as per market references provided by [Sherlock]([URL] and [Zealynx]([URL] The total commitments are expected to reach ~$2M once in-progress and pending audits are activated.

### What Worked

- **The program delivered on its original mandate.** With ~60% of funded teams net new to the ecosystem, it attracted security-first founders who might otherwise have launched elsewhere.

- **It demonstrated [PROJECT]'s dedication to user security.** Funding security work upfront led to tangible critical findings, remediated before mainnet.

- **Operationally the program matured.** A growing referral channel now drives roughly half of onboarded teams, and pricing has stayed within benchmarked ranges.

### Lessons Learned

- **Early-stage teams didn't have enough runway to benefit from audits.** Some recipients were unable to move forward after receiving funding, in a few cases winding down within months. Future eligibility should require at least 1 year of runway and the capacity to cover part of the audit cost.

- **Value secured has concentrated in later-stage teams** that could typically fund audits themselves - a tension with the early-stage mandate, since younger projects generally need more time to grow TVL for their product.

- **Lead times are long.** Audit contract signature to mainnet launch averages ~135 days for teams not yet live.

- **Impact was real, but visibility was low.** Audit subsidies set [PROJECT] apart from other ecosystems, but the program received too little visibility to capitalize on that. Going forward, funded teams will be asked to publicly acknowledge the subsidy, among other improvements to program communications.

These results and lessons, among others, shape the adjustments below.

## Specifications

### Program Adjustments

#### 1. Expand Scope with AI Audits

AAP identified five AI security agents to be trialed under this program. ASP will run the pilot: every funded team will receive an AI-assisted review ahead of its full audit, with lower-cost AI screening available to earlier-stage teams, and all five tools running in parallel for evaluation.

#### 2. Expand Scope with Core Protocol Security: Bug Bounty & Security Council

Audits are point-in-time; protecting the core protocol that every funded team builds on also requires continuous review of live code and emergency response - the program's third and fourth pillars:

- **Bug Bounty (continuous review).** [PROJECT] operates a [bug bounty]([URL] covering the [PROJECT] One and [PROJECT] Nova smart contracts, with rewards of up to $2,000,000 for critical findings - a maximum that has never been paid out since the Foundation began running the program. Its scope remains the [PROJECT] protocol codebase; ecosystem teams' codebases are covered through the AI-screening and audit pathway above.

- **Security Council (emergency response).** The ArbitrumDAO Security Council is the DAO-elected body empowered by the Constitution to respond to security emergencies affecting the protocol in production, and has been historically funded by the AF on behalf of the DAO.

Both are included for the reason set out in the Abstract: redirecting part of the unspent allocation toward the security layers with the highest impact on the ecosystem - every team, user, and dollar of TVL on [PROJECT] ultimately depends on the integrity of the core protocol they protect - with no change to the bounty's scope and reward terms or to the Council's compensation, election process, and constitutional mandate. Bug and bounty reporting will be provided yearly at a high level, e.g., total payout amounts.

#### 3. Maintain Alignment Framework

After strict exclusivity created material friction during AAP, the requirement was revised via a [formal governance proposal]([URL] into a DAO-approved, alignment-based framework, which ASP adopts as its baseline.

#### 4. Introduce a Lightweight Governance Process

Adjusting the exclusivity framework during AAP showed that putting every program change through the full governance process adds significant overhead. ASP therefore adopts the optimistic approval framework from the recent [Code of Conduct proposal]([URL] changes posted to the forum by the AF take effect after 14 days unless a combined 5% of delegated VP (measured at the time of posting) raises objections, in which case the change goes to an off-chain vote at the non-constitutional quorum. The AF is responsible for monitoring objections and tallying VP.

#### 5. Enable Idle Funds Deployment

Lastly, with the majority of AAP funds remaining unproductive for the duration of the program, we propose that ASP deploy idle funds into low-risk management strategies.

## Budget

AAP was funded through a 30M [TOKEN] allocation, part of which was converted to cover audit commitments and the $60k technical expert retainer; roughly $1.23M was committed by the end of Q3, expected to reach ~$2M by program close (cumulative over the program's duration). ASP requests no new funding: it operates from the actual remaining balance already held by the Foundation - $1.76M USDC plus 25M [TOKEN] - less ~$1.2M in predicted outstanding deployments (final amount depends on total audit commitments, some of which may not materialize). This budget covers the expanded scope:

- Audit, AI screening and security subsidies for ecosystem teams.

- [PROJECT] protocol bug bounties: operation of the bug bounty program, with contingent reward payouts for validated findings.

- Security Council: member compensation of $5,000 per member per month across the 12-member Council, i.e., $720,000 per year.

- Technical expert: retainer of $2,500/month (down from $5,000/month, or $60,000/year, in AAP), reflecting updated workload.

- All other costs (legal, program management, operations) remain covered by the [PROJECT] Foundation.

As in AAP, funds committed towards audits will be disclosed in each quarterly transparency report, giving the DAO visibility into deployment pace against the remaining balance. Any balance unspent at term end returns to the ArbitrumDAO treasury unless the DAO approves a continuation.

## Timeline

With AAP applications closed on [DATE] and an approximate two-month wind-down underway, continuity of a live audit offering is an important matter for builders on [PROJECT]. We propose the following governance timeline, subject to delegate feedback:

- [DATE] → Proposal posted in the forum (complete)

- [DATE] → Binding off-chain vote following non-constitutional quorum

- By [DATE] → Applications open for the program, with an official announcement declaring the start date and the one-year clock.

All candidates that applied have passed the preliminary eligibility check and will therefore participate in the elections. ### Application of Code of Conduct in the OAT Election

The 'Responsible Voting Policy' that was present in the first OAT election is no longer part of the [Code of Conduct]([URL] or the [DAO's procedures]([URL] so delegates can spread their voting power however they wish. Delegates and participating candidates who seek to abstain from the vote can do so by voting in a neutral manner, e.g., by splitting the voting power equally across all candidates to effectively abstain.

Titel: [Ethereum] [PROJECT] Liquidity Layer - Set Ethena sUSDe Rate Limits to 0

# [Ethereum] [PROJECT] Liquidity Layer - Set Ethena sUSDe Rate Limits to 0 - [DATE]

[PROJECT]'s Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The [PROJECT] community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

To complete the offboarding of Ethena, included in the [[[DATE]] Proposed Changes to [PROJECT] for Upcoming Spell]([URL] proposal and approved in the [[DATE] Snapshot Poll]([URL] this proposal removes the rate limit to deposit USDe into sUSDe (4626 deposit) that was not marked for deprecation and sets this rate limit to 0 alongside the other Ethena rate limits.

### Required Context

This change was missed in the [[[DATE]] Proposed Changes to [PROJECT] for Upcoming Spell]([URL] proposal, as part of item 1, [Ethereum] [PROJECT] Liquidity Layer - Offboard Unused Integrations, as indicated in the [comment from the author of the proposal]([URL] This proposal rectifies that omission.

### Proposed Actions

Fully offboard Ethena USDe/sUSDe, by changing the Ethena sUSDe inflow rate limits as follows:

- `maxAmount`: 250,000,000 → 0 USDe
- `slope`: 100,000,000 → 0 USDe per day

The proposed [PROJECT] Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: [URL]

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into [PROJECT]'s artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

Titel: [Ethereum] [PROJECT] Liquidity Layer - Offboard Unused Integrations

# [Ethereum] [PROJECT] Liquidity Layer - Offboard Unused Integrations - [DATE]

[PROJECT]'s Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The [PROJECT] community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

If approved, this proposal will offboard a set of unused integrations by zeroing their rate limits, removing standing relayer authority over venues [PROJECT] no longer uses.

Each live rate limit is standing authority for the relayer to move funds to or from a venue. Where [PROJECT] has no position and no intention of using a venue again, that authority is unearned risk surface. Zeroing the limits removes it without moving any funds.

### Required Context

**How an SLL rate limit is disabled**: `RateLimits.setRateLimitData(key, 0, 0)`. There is no removal function; a zeroed limit makes any controller call touching that key revert at `require(maxAmount > 0, "RateLimits/zero-maxAmount")` inside `triggerRateLimitDecrease`. Rate-limit keys are derived as `keccak256(abi.encode(LIMIT_BASE, venue))`, except the five bare keys (`LIMIT_USDE_MINT`, `LIMIT_USDE_BURN`, `LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN`, `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_SUBSCRIBE`, and the orphaned `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_REDEEM`), which bind to a single immutable set in the controller's constructor and therefore use the bare `keccak256("LIMIT_X")` as the storage key.

**Proposal's scope is 34 rate-limit keys**, covering both the integrations [PROJECT] has already exited and those it had kept available but has now decided not to use. Twenty-one belong to the integrations previously confirmed for offboarding and thirteen to those previously held open as candidates; the per-key detail is in [Proposed actions, Item 1]([URL] Two venues need fewer keys than they appear to: the Curve PYUSD/USDC and Curve USDC/USDT deposit and withdraw limits are **already zero** (the former was never configured; the latter was zeroed on [DATE]), so only their swap legs need action.

**Superstate is offboarded in full, and that takes five keys rather than two.** The subscription and redemption paths are asymmetric, and the redemption rails are easy to miss because they are **self-transfers** — `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER(asset, asset)` — used to trigger burn-on-transfer redemption, rather than transfers between an asset and a stablecoin:

  | Path | Key | Current |
  | :---- | :---- | :---- |
  | USTB subscribe | `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_SUBSCRIBE` (bare) | 300,000,000 USDC, 100M/day |
  | USTB redeem | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER(USTB, USTB)` | unlimited |
  | USCC subscribe | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER(USDC, USCC_DEPOSIT)` | 100,000,000 USDC, 50M/day |
  | USCC redeem | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER(USCC, USCC)` | unlimited |
  | USTB redeem (legacy) | `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_REDEEM` (bare) | unlimited |

The last of these is **an orphaned storage entry**: `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_REDEEM` is not among the twenty-nine `LIMIT_*` constants declared by the deployed v1.10.0 controller, so no live code path reads it. It is zeroed anyway as a defensive measure — the value persists in `RateLimits` storage independently of the controller, so if a future controller version reintroduced that constant, a stale unlimited limit would become live immediately. The three `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` legs pointing at the registry's `SUPERSTATE_REDEMPTION` address were checked and are **already zero**, having never been configured; they need no action. The ALM Proxy holds **0 USTB and 0 USCC**, so Superstate is a clean exit with no residual.

**The Proposal deliberately leaves residual balances behind.** Several offboarded venues still hold small ALM Proxy positions. These are not withdrawn, before or during the spell: the amounts are below the marginal cost of retrieving them, and any of them can be recovered later by a dedicated spell if that ever becomes worthwhile. Both the deposit and withdraw sides are zeroed. The precedent and its consequence are both known — roughly 300 USD has been stranded in Base Fluid sUSDS since the equivalent [MONTH] [YEAR] zeroing.

### Proposed Actions

**34 calls to `RateLimits.setRateLimitData(key, 0, 0)`** on [`eth:[ADDRESS]`]([URL] executed as the [PROJECT] SubDAO Proxy, which holds `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`. **No funds move.** Keys are derived as `keccak256(abi.encode(LIMIT_BASE, venue))`, or `keccak256(abi.encode(LIMIT_BASE, asset, destination))` for transfer legs, except the five bare keys which use the bare `keccak256("LIMIT_X")`.

**Parameters, and their current values read at block 25,807,000:**

| # | Venue | Key derivation | Current `maxAmount` / slope | After |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Morpho v1 DAI vault | `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT` × vault | 200,000,000 DAI / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 2 | Morpho v1 DAI vault | `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW` × vault | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 3 | Morpho v1 USDS vault | `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT` × vault | 200,000,000 USDS / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 4 | Morpho v1 USDS vault | `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW` × vault | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 5 | Aave Core aEthUSDe | `LIMIT_AAVE_DEPOSIT` × aToken | 250,000,000 USDe / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 6 | Aave Core aEthUSDe | `LIMIT_AAVE_WITHDRAW` × aToken | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 7 | Ethena USDe mint | `LIMIT_USDE_MINT` (global) | 250,000,000 USDC / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 8 | Ethena USDe burn | `LIMIT_USDE_BURN` (global) | 500,000,000 USDe / 200M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 9 | Ethena sUSDe cooldown | `LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN` (global) | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 10–12 | Maple syrupUSDT | `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT`, `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW`, `LIMIT_MAPLE_REDEEM` × token | 50,000,000 USDT / unlimited / unlimited | `0 / 0` each |
| 13–15 | Maple syrupUSDC | same three keys × token | 100,000,000 USDC / unlimited / unlimited | `0 / 0` each |
| 16–18 | Curve PYUSD/USDS | `LIMIT_CURVE_DEPOSIT`, `_WITHDRAW`, `_SWAP` × pool | 5,000,000 / 5,000,000 / 5,000,000 | `0 / 0` each |
| 19 | Curve PYUSD/USDC | `LIMIT_CURVE_SWAP` × pool | 5,000,000 | `0 / 0` |
